standard.name: MIMARKS (Minimum Information about a Marker Gene Sequence)
standard.abstract: MIMARKS defines metadata fields for marker gene sequence studies (nucleic acid sequence reports) describing samples and sequencing experiments from diverse environments. The checklist covers investigation-level metadata (project, investigation type), environmental/sample descriptors (latitude/longitude, depth, elevation, geographic names, biome), temporal information (collection date), and submission indicators. Values are recorded as structured comment fields for sequence archives and are intended to accompany sequencing data (SRA/ENA/DDBJ/GenBank).

classification.rationale: The source is an explicit worksheet presenting a row-based checklist of named metadata fields with concrete value syntaxes (e.g. {boolean}, {text}, {timestamp}, {float}) and occurrence rules — i.e. a genuine metadata table.

submitted_to_insdc.name: submitted to insdc
submitted_to_insdc.descr: Depending on the study (large-scale e.g. done with next generation sequencing technology, or small-scale) sequences have to be submitted to SRA (Sequence Read Archive), DRA (DDBJ Read Archive) or via the classical Webin/Sequin systems to Genbank, ENA and DDBJ
submitted_to_insdc.evidence:
Depending on the study (large-scale e.g. done with next generation sequencing technology, or small-scale) sequences have to be submitted to SRA (Sequence Read Archive), DRA (DDBJ Read Archive) or via the classical Webin/Sequin systems to Genbank, ENA and DDBJ

Value syntax: {boolean}

investigation_type.name: investigation type
investigation_type.descr: Nucleic Acid Sequence Report is the root element of all MIGS/MIMS compliant reports as standardized by Genomic Standards Consortium. This field is either eukaryote,bacteria,virus,plasmid,organelle, metagenome, mimarks-survey or mimarks-culture
investigation_type.evidence:
Nucleic Acid Sequence Report is the root element of all MIGS/MIMS compliant reports as standardized by Genomic Standards Consortium. This field is either eukaryote,bacteria,virus,plasmid,organelle, metagenome, mimarks-survey or mimarks-culture

Value syntax: [eukaryote|bacteria_archaea|plasmid|virus|organelle|metagenome,mimarks-survey|mimarks-culture]

project_name.name: project name
project_name.descr: Name of the project within which the sequencing was organized
project_name.evidence:
Name of the project within which the sequencing was organized

Value syntax: {text}

experimental_factor.name: experimental factor
experimental_factor.descr: Experimental factors are essentially the variable aspects of an experiment design which can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI).
experimental_factor.evidence:
Experimental factors are essentially the variable aspects of an experiment design which can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI). For a browser of EFO (v132) terms, please see http://bioportal.bioontology.org/visualize/44641; for a browser of OBI (v1.0) terms please see http://bioportal.bioontology.org/visualize/40832

Value syntax: {term|text}

lat_lon.name: geographic location (latitude and longitude)
lat_lon.descr: The geographical origin of the sample as defined by latitude and longitude. The values should be reported in decimal degrees and in WGS84 system
lat_lon.evidence:
The geographical origin of the sample as defined by latitude and longitude. The values should be reported in decimal degrees and in WGS84 system

Value syntax: {float} {float}

depth.name: geographic location (depth)
depth.descr: Please refer to the definitions of depth in the environmental packages
depth.evidence:
Please refer to the definitions of depth in the environmental packages

Value syntax: -

alt_elev.name: geographic location (altitude/elevation)
alt_elev.descr: Please refer to the definitions of either altitude or elevation in the environmental packages
alt_elev.evidence:
Please refer to the definitions of either altitude or elevation in the environmental packages

Value syntax: -

geo_loc_name.name: geographic location (country and/or sea,region)
geo_loc_name.descr: The geographical origin of the sample as defined by the country or sea name followed by specific region name. Country or sea names should be chosen from the INSDC country list (http://insdc.org/country.html), or the GAZ ontology (v1.446) (http://bioportal.bioontology.org/visualize/40651)

collection_date.name: collection date
collection_date.descr: The time of sampling, either as an instance (single point in time) or interval. In case no exact time is available, the date/time can be right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23T19:23:10+00:00; 2008-01-23T19:23:10; 2008-01-23; 2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant
collection_date.evidence:
The time of sampling, either as an instance (single point in time) or interval. In case no exact time is available, the date/time can be right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23T19:23:10+00:00; 2008-01-23T19:23:10; 2008-01-23; 2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant

Value syntax: {timestamp}

biome.name: environment (biome)
biome.descr: In environmental biome level are the major classes of ecologically similar communities of plants, animals, and other organisms. Biomes are defined based on factors such as plant structures, leaf types, plant spacing, and other factors like climate.
biome.evidence: In environmental biome level are the major classes of ecologically similar communities of plants, animals, and other organisms. Biomes are defined based on factors such as plant structures, leaf types, plant spacing, and other factors like climate.

standard.notes: Extracted fields correspond to rows present in the provided MIMARKS worksheet excerpt. Some fields (e.g. depth, alt_elev) delegate exact syntax/units to environment-specific packages and the worksheet shows '-' for value syntax; these were represented as string types here with the original value-syntax preserved in raw_full_info.
